Not independently confirmed (verify the figure): Credit for Low-Income Household Renters; Credit for Child and Dependent Care Expenses.
_strings.@@1b090f3f0709: Print only the form pages (not instructions), single-sided; attach state copies of W-2/1099.
_strings.@@3dd41a76cc7b: Refundable Earned Income Tax Credit (Hawaii EITC) — A qualifying individual taxpayer who (a) files a federal return and claims the federal earned income credit under IRC section 32 for the tax year, (b) uses the same filing status on the Hawaii return as on the federal return, and (c) claims the same dependents on the Hawaii return as on the federal return. Part-year residents and nonresidents prorate by the ratio of Hawaii AGI to federal AGI.
_strings.@@42a5342f7d0a: Hawaii Form N-11 (Rev. 2023) Individual Income Tax Return (Resident) — line 7 'Federal adjusted gross income (AGI)' and line 10 'Other Hawaii Additions to federal AGI'
_strings.@@4d42ad525021: Mailing address: Some state facts could not be independently re-confirmed — see the pack's `unverified` list; confirm at the cited DOR source before relying on a specific figure/address.
_strings.@@7325e141f0b6: Hawaii Department of Taxation, P.O. Box 3559, Honolulu, Hawaii 96811-3559 (use when NOT enclosing a check or money order)
_strings.@@a2f3f69ba762: Credit for Child and Dependent Care Expenses — Taxpayers who paid qualified expenses for the care of a qualifying person (e.g., dependent child or disabled dependent/spouse) to enable them (and a spouse, if married) to work or look for work, including payments to the State of Hawaii A+ Program. Generally married persons must file jointly; married-filing-separately taxpayers may claim only if they meet the separate-filer requirements in the instructions. Provider information must be reported on Schedule X, Part II.
_strings.@@a7f838172c61: Credit for Low-Income Household Renters — Hawaii resident present in Hawaii more than nine months during 2023 who occupies and pays rent for real property in Hawaii used as a residence, whose rental unit was fully subject to real property tax (units wholly or partially exempt do not qualify), and who is not (and is not eligible to be) claimed as a dependent by another taxpayer. Net rent paid (after exclusions such as utilities, parking, ground rent, and rental subsidies/public assistance) must exceed $1,000.
_strings.@@af5076e0dfcb: Form N-15, Individual Income Tax Return — Nonresident and Part-Year Resident (Rev. 2023)
_strings.@@b4482444b5e8: Refundable Food/Excise Tax Credit — Each individual income tax filer (including those with no taxable income) who is a Hawaii resident physically present in Hawaii more than nine months during 2023, who is not (and is not eligible to be) claimed as a dependent by another taxpayer for federal or Hawaii purposes, and who is not incarcerated for the entire year. Credit is computed per qualified exemption (taxpayer, spouse, dependents, plus certain minor children receiving public support).
_strings.@@c918be354b24: Treaty conformity — HI conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from HI income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the HI return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Hawaii's resident return (Form N-11) line 7 starts from "Federal adjusted gross income (AGI)" reported from federal Form 1040/1040-SR. Treaty-exempt income excluded at the federal level is therefore already excluded from the Hawaii starting amount. Hawaii's additions to federal AGI are an explicit, enumerated list on Form N-11 line 10 ("Other Hawaii Additions to Federal AGI"): differences in the taxable portion of the Hawaii tax refund, Individual Housing Account distributions, Peace Corps compensation, depreciation/gain differences, compensation from temporary employment outside the United States, student-loan-interest differences, employer-provided adoption-benefit differences, qualified tuition program distributions for K-12, distributions from certain foreign corporations, and "other adjustments." None of these is an add-back of federal tax-treaty-exempt income (unlike California's Schedule CA). The N-11 instructions' "Special Instructions for Nonresident Aliens" further state that a person who is a nonresident alien for federal purposes but a Hawaii resident applies the federal nonresident-alien rules when filing the Hawaii resident return and still begins from federal AGI, with no instruction to add back treaty income. Conclusion: treaty-exempt income is NOT re-taxed -> conforms = true.
_strings.@@eb71823a243b: Multi-state income allocation (which dollars belong to which state) is your and the user's judgment; this tool scopes the returns and supplies the rules/warnings, not the allocation.

This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Printed-constant divergence: the schedules print whole-dollar base-tax constants (e.g. $34 at $2,400 vs exact $33.60), so the filed schedule can differ from exact marginal math by up to $1; the tax TABLE is mandated below $100,000 taxable income. Schedule structure: II = exactly 2x Schedule I boundaries, III = exactly 1.5x — verified digit-by-digit from the printed schedules.
